title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the neighbouring pages: S is a base scheme. M is a rank-4 Azumaya algebra over O_S, i.e. a form of M_2(O_S), typically M = End_{O_S}(F) with F locally free of rank 2. The groups are G = M^* (a form of GL_2), SG (the norm-1 elements, a form of SL_2) and PG (a form of PGL_2). A section of M is 'regular' if it is nowhere a scalar in any fibre. The previous page characterised regular unipotent elements ε = 1+N.

This page does the same for rank-one idempotents. For a section P of M the following are equivalent:
(a) P is regular and P² = P.
(b) det P = 0 and Tr P = 1.
(c) Locally there is a basis (e_0, e_1) of F in which P = diag(0,1), i.e. P is the projection of O e_0 ⊕ O e_1 onto O e_1.
(c') P is a projector whose image D_1 and kernel D_0 are both of rank 1.
(d) Zariski-locally there is an isomorphism M_2(O_S) → M sending diag(0,1) to P.

The key implication is (b) ⇒ (a).
- Cayley–Hamilton gives P² − (Tr P)P + det P = 0, hence P² = P.
- Regularity holds because if P were a scalar λ in some fibre, then λ² = 0 and 2λ = 1. So λ would be invertible and nilpotent, which is absurd.
- Generalisation: if the discriminant of the characteristic polynomial, δ(ρ) = (Tr ρ)² − 4 det ρ, is a unit of O_S, then ρ is regular, since a fibrewise scalar has δ = 0. For P this discriminant equals 1.

Such P are named 'projecteurs élémentaires'. Corollary: elementary projectors correspond bijectively to Killing couples (B, T), with T a maximal torus contained in the Borel B, in G (or SG, or PG). P determines the splitting F = D_0 ⊕ D_1. T is the centraliser of P (the diagonal torus); B is the stabiliser of D_0. The opposite couple (stabiliser of D_1) corresponds to 1 − P.

The next page goes on to the geometry of these schemes over the scheme of Borels. Their fibre product over that scheme is isomorphic to the scheme of pinnings (épinglages). This is preparatory material, setting up the GL_2 / SL_2 / PGL_2 forms used in the 'équation des lacets' part of the Longue Marche notes.
errors: Minor: the remark implicitly uses fibres being nonempty (λ invertible and square-zero is absurd only on a nonzero fibre); this is trivially fine.
Minor: 2λ = 1 forces 2 to be invertible in that fibre; the argument covers this, since in characteristic 2 the equation 2λ = 1 is impossible, so no scalar λ exists there either.
On the next page the associated projector of the opposite couple is written '1−N'; it should be 1−P (a notational slip).

ideas.what: Rank-one idempotents in a rank-4 Azumaya algebra characterised by det = 0, Tr = 1, and their local normal form diag(0,1)
ideas.modern_name: rank-one idempotents / splitting of quaternion (Azumaya) algebras by an idempotent
ideas.where_published: Le groupe de Brauer I-II treats Azumaya algebras in general, but not this specific statement

ideas.what: An invertible discriminant of the characteristic polynomial implies regularity (nowhere scalar)
ideas.modern_name: regular semisimple elements of GL_2 forms

ideas.what: Bijection between elementary projectors and Killing couples (B, T); opposite couple ↔ 1 − P
ideas.modern_name: Killing couples / pairs (Borel, maximal torus) for forms of GL_2

deep.surprise_reason: Routine linear algebra over a base scheme, recasting SGA3 notions for forms of GL_2 as preparation for the Longue Marche material; nothing new.
transcription_corrections: 'donc ρ est une section régulière' — the conclusion word is likely 'alors' or 'donc'; immaterial.
The isolated 'Ens.' after the Definition is probably an abbreviation (e.g. 'Ens.' = ensemble/schéma des P); uncertain.
In d) the margin insertion is '(loc. Zar)' attached to ∃; the arrow is an isomorphism M ← M_2(O_S).
